_note: 원문 유형은 문장 삽입. insert 유형을 가장 강하게 출제. 유형마다 passage 를 다르게 paraphrase.

passage: Does moving your hands as you describe an event help you remember that event better?
We showed adults videos of objects, animals, and people doing strange little actions.
Afterward we tested their memory of these events, both right away and three weeks later.
Adults told to gesture while describing the events recalled more than those told to keep still.
To check whether spontaneous gesturing worked too, we ran the study again with no instructions.
We found the same pattern: people remembered the items they had gestured about more clearly.
Producing gesture along with speech makes the information in that speech easier to remember.
choices: why some actions in videos are stranger than others
how adults and children differ in their memory of stories
how gesturing while describing events strengthens our memory of them
why speaking slowly helps listeners understand difficult ideas
how watching videos improves the brain's overall health
theme.explanation_ko: 사건을 묘사하며 제스처한 성인이 더 잘 기억했고, 자발적 제스처에서도 같은 결과가 나와 제스처가 기억을 돕는다는 내용. ③이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①영상 속 이상한 동작, ②성인·아동 차이, ④느린 말하기, ⑤영상의 건강 효과는 본문의 핵심이 아니다.

passage: We should not treat hand gestures as mere decoration that adds nothing to our words.
In our study, adults watched videos of objects, animals, and people doing odd actions.
Those told to gesture while describing the events later remembered more than those who stayed still.
We must recognize that the body takes part in remembering, not just the tongue.
When we repeated the study without instructions, spontaneous gesturers showed the same advantage.
People recalled best exactly the items they had gestured about on their own.
We ought to use gesture deliberately, since it makes spoken information stick in the mind.
Moving as we speak is not a distraction but a genuine aid to memory.
choices: 어려운 동작일수록 영상으로 보여 주어야 한다.
기억력을 높이려면 같은 영상을 여러 번 반복해서 봐야 한다.
말을 천천히 할수록 듣는 사람이 더 잘 이해한다.
손동작은 의사소통을 방해하므로 자제하는 것이 좋다.
제스처는 말의 내용을 더 잘 기억하게 하므로 의도적으로 활용해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 제스처가 말의 내용을 더 잘 기억하게 하므로 의도적으로 활용해야 한다는 주장. ⑤가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①영상, ②반복 시청, ③느린 말하기, ④손동작 자제는 본문 주장과 어긋나거나 무관하다.

passage: Can moving your hands as you describe something help you remember it later?
Adults in our study watched videos of objects, animals, and people doing odd things.
We tested their memory of these events right away and again three weeks later.
Those told to gesture while describing remembered more than those told not to.
When we removed the instructions, people who gestured on their own did just as well.
They best recalled the very items they had naturally gestured about.
Gesturing along with speech makes the spoken information more memorable.
choices: 영상 속 동작이 이상할수록 더 오래 기억된다.
기억은 시간이 지날수록 점점 더 또렷해진다.
손동작은 말의 의미를 흐리게 만든다.
말하면서 제스처를 하면 그 내용을 더 잘 기억하게 된다.
성인은 아동보다 영상을 더 잘 기억한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 지시받은 제스처든 자발적 제스처든, 제스처와 함께 묘사한 내용을 더 잘 기억한다는 것이 요지. ④가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①이상한 동작, ②시간 경과, ③의미 흐림, ⑤성인·아동 비교는 요지가 아니다.

passage: Could the simple act of moving your hands help lock a memory into place?
We had adults watch short videos of objects, animals, and people doing odd little actions.
Then we tested their memory of those events, immediately and three weeks later.
People who gestured while describing the events remembered far more than those who did not.
Repeating the study without instructions, we watched who gestured on their own.
Once again, the gestured items were the best remembered.
Hands, it seems, help the mind hold on to what the mouth has said.
choices: Why Some Videos Are Easier to Watch Than Others
Talking with Your Hands: How Gesture Helps Us Remember
The Strange Actions That Confuse the Human Brain
How to Speak Clearly Without Moving at All
Memory Loss: Why We Forget Within Three Weeks
title.explanation_ko: 제스처가 말의 내용을 더 잘 기억하게 한다는 핵심을 압축한 ②가 제목.
title.distractor_ko: ①영상 시청, ③이상한 동작, ④움직이지 않는 말하기, ⑤망각은 글의 초점이 아니다.

passage: We wondered whether the hands could help the memory do its work.
Adults watched videos of objects, animals, and people performing strange little actions.
We tested their memory of these events right away and again weeks later.
Those who gestured while describing remembered more than those who held their hands still.
Even when no one was told to gesture, the spontaneous gesturers showed the same advantage.
The items they had gestured about were the ones that stayed with them.
It seems the moving hand quietly writes the memory more deeply.
implication.underlined: the moving hand quietly writes the memory more deeply
choices: people who write things down remember them better than others
hand muscles grow stronger each time we recall an event
silence is the best way to store a new memory
gesturing while speaking helps fix information more firmly in memory
only unusual actions are worth remembering at all
implication.explanation_ko: '움직이는 손이 기억을 더 깊이 새긴다'는 비유는 말하며 제스처하면 정보가 기억에 더 단단히 자리 잡는다는 뜻이다. ④가 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ①필기, ②근육, ③침묵, ⑤이상한 동작은 비유의 의미와 다르다.

passage: If you gesture while describing an event, do you think you will recall it better?
We had adults watched videos of objects, animals, and people performing odd actions.
We then tested the adults' memories of these events immediately and three weeks later.
Adults who were told to gesture remembered more than adults who were told not to.
To see if we would get the same effects, we did the study again with no instructions.
We found the same patterns: people remembered items on which they had gestured spontaneously.
Producing gesture along with speech makes the information encoded in that speech memorable.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
grammar.explanation_ko: ② 사역동사 had 의 목적격보어 자리이므로 과거형 'watched' 가 아니라 원형부정사 'watch' 가 와야 한다('had adults watch'). ②가 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①접속사+분사 while describing, ③be told 뒤 진목적어 역할의 to부정사 to gesture, ④목적의 to부정사 To see, ⑤동사 had gestured 를 수식하는 부사 spontaneously 는 모두 옳다.

passage: If you gesture while describing an event, you may recall it better than if you stay still.
We had adults watch videos of objects, animals, and people performing odd actions.
We then tested their memories of these events immediately and three weeks later.
Adults told to gesture forgot more than adults told not to, especially weeks later.
To see if we would get the same effects, we repeated the study with no instructions.
We found the same patterns: people remembered the gestured items better than the others.
Producing gesture along with speech makes the information in that speech more memorable.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
vocab.explanation_ko: ③ 제스처가 기억을 돕는다는 글의 흐름상, 제스처하라고 들은 성인이 그러지 말라고 들은 성인보다 '더 많이 기억했다(remembered)'여야 한다. '더 많이 잊었다(forgot)'는 정반대 의미라 부적절하므로 remembered 로 고쳐야 한다. ③이 정답.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①recall(기억해 내다), ②tested(검사했다), ④repeated(반복했다), ⑤better(더 잘)는 문맥에 적절하다.

blank.explanation_ko: 지시 없이 자발적으로 제스처한 사람들도 그 항목을 가장 잘 기억했으므로, 자발적 제스처도 똑같이 기억을 도왔다는 결과이다. ③이 정답.

We then tested the adults' memories of these events immediately and again three weeks later.
Adults told to gesture while describing the events remembered more than adults told not to.
Many professional actors use deep breathing exercises to calm their nerves before a performance.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '제스처가 기억을 돕는다'는 실험 흐름인데 ④ '배우의 호흡 운동으로 긴장 완화'는 무관하다.

order.given: If you gesture while describing an event, do you think you will recall that event better than if you don't gesture? We had adults watch videos of objects, animals, and people performing various, sometimes odd, actions.

blocks.A: Adults who were told to gesture while describing the events remembered more than adults who were told not to gesture, particularly several weeks later.
blocks.B: We then tested the adults' memories of these events immediately after the descriptions and again three weeks later.
blocks.C: To see if we would get the same effects when people gestured on their own, we did the study again, but this time we gave the adults no instructions about gesture. We found the same patterns.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글이 영상 시청을 소개하면, (B)가 'then ... tested(그 후 검사했다)'로 기억 검사를, (A)가 그 검사 결과(제스처 집단이 더 잘 기억함)를, (C)가 'To see ... same effects' 로 자발적 제스처 후속 실험을 잇는다. (B)-(A)-(C).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 'same effects(같은 효과)'는 (A)의 첫 결과 이후라야 하고, (A)의 결과는 (B)의 검사 다음에 와야 한다.

insert.insert_sentence: Adults who were told to gesture while describing the events remembered more than adults who were told not to gesture, particularly several weeks later.

passage_marked.text: If you gesture while describing an event, do you think you will recall it better than if you don't?
We had adults watch videos of objects, animals, and people performing various, sometimes odd, actions.
We then tested the adults' memories of these events immediately and again three weeks later.
To see if we would get the same effects when people gestured on their own, we did the study again with no instructions.
We found the same patterns: people remembered items on which they had gestured spontaneously better than items on which they had not.

choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 첫 실험의 '결과(제스처 집단이 더 잘 기억함)'이므로, 기억을 검사했다는 ③ 다음, 그리고 '같은 효과가 나는지 보려고' 후속 실험을 했다는 문장 앞에 와야 한다. ③이 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ③에 넣지 않으면 'To see if we would get the same effects' 의 'same effects(같은 효과)'가 가리킬 첫 실험 결과가 앞에 나타나지 않는다.

passage: We asked whether gesturing while describing an event improves later memory of it.
Adults watched videos of objects, animals, and people doing odd actions.
We tested their memory immediately and three weeks later.
Those told to gesture remembered more than those told to stay still.
Repeating the study without instructions, we watched spontaneous gesturers.
They too remembered the gestured items best.
Gesture along with speech makes spoken information more memorable.
summary.summary_template: Whether people gestured on instruction or __(A)__, they remembered the described events better, suggesting that gesture __(B)__ memory.
summary.explanation_ko: 지시받든 (A)자발적으로(spontaneously) 하든 제스처한 사건을 더 잘 기억했으므로, 제스처가 기억을 (B)강화한다(strengthens). ⑤.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 rarely/silently 가 아니라 spontaneously, (B)는 weakens/blocks/erases 가 아니라 strengthens 여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 우리는 그 후 이 사건들에 대한 성인들의 기억을 검사했다.
writing.answer: We then tested the adults' memories of these events.
writing.explanation_ko: 부사 then + 동사 tested + 목적어 the adults' memories of these events.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 말과 함께 제스처를 산출하는 것은 그 정보를 기억하기 쉽게 만든다.
writing.answer: Producing gesture along with speech makes the information memorable.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사 주어 Producing gesture along with speech + makes + 목적어 the information + 목적격보어 memorable.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 제스처하라고 들은 성인들이 그러지 말라고 들은 성인들보다 더 많이 기억했다.
conditions: 주격 관계대명사 who 를 두 번 사용할 것
비교급 more ~ than 을 사용할 것
writing.answer: Adults who were told to gesture remembered more than adults who were told not to.
writing.explanation_ko: 주격 관계대명사 who were told + 비교급 remembered more than + who were told not to.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: To see if we would get the same effects when people gestured on their own, we did the study again with no ___________ about gesture.
writing.explanation_ko: 자발적 제스처를 보려고 제스처에 관한 '지시(instructions)' 없이 다시 실험했다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: We found the same patterns: people remembered items on which they had gestured spontaneously better than items on which they had not gestured.
writing.answer: 우리는 같은 패턴을 발견했다. 사람들은 자신이 자발적으로 제스처했던 항목을 제스처하지 않았던 항목보다 더 잘 기억했다.
writing.explanation_ko: 전치사+관계대명사 on which, gestured spontaneously(자발적으로 제스처했다), better than(~보다 더 잘).
